setup: CREATE FUNCTION issuance_service.synthetic_terminal_barrier() RETURNS trigger LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$ BEGIN PERFORM pg_advisory_xact_lock(814,51); INSERT INTO issuance_service.synthetic_terminal_writes(status) VALUES(NEW.status); RETURN NEW; END $$

CREATE TRIGGER synthetic_terminal_barrier BEFORE UPDATE OF status ON issuance_service.canvas_evidence_sync_jobs FOR EACH ROW WHEN (OLD.id='worker-final-job' AND OLD.status='leased' AND NEW.status IN ('succeeded','dead_letter')) EXECUTE FUNCTION issuance_service.synthetic_terminal_barrier()
terminal_wait_sql: SELECT count(*)=1 FROM pg_locks WHERE locktype='advisory' AND classid=814 AND objid=51 AND NOT granted AND database=(SELECT oid FROM pg_database WHERE datname=current_database())
reclaimer_wait_sql: WITH RECURSIVE blockers(pid,path) AS (SELECT a.pid,ARRAY[a.pid] FROM pg_stat_activity a WHERE a.datname=current_database() AND a.usename='synthetic_reclaimer' AND a.state='active' AND a.wait_event_type='Lock' AND a.wait_event IN ('tuple','transactionid') AND a.query LIKE '%canvas_evidence_sync_jobs%' UNION ALL SELECT p.pid,b.path||p.pid FROM blockers b CROSS JOIN LATERAL unnest(pg_blocking_pids(b.pid)) AS p(pid) WHERE NOT p.pid=ANY(b.path)) SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM blockers b JOIN pg_locks l ON l.pid=b.pid WHERE l.locktype='advisory' AND l.classid=814 AND l.objid=51 AND NOT l.granted AND l.database=(SELECT oid FROM pg_database WHERE datname=current_database()))
job_row_sql: SELECT to_jsonb(j) FROM issuance_service.canvas_evidence_sync_jobs j WHERE id='worker-final-job'
target_row_sql: SELECT to_jsonb(t) FROM issuance_service.canvas_evidence_sync_targets t WHERE id='target-review'
scope: Actual provider/process completion owns the terminal job write before real lease expiry; another actual process attempts recovery. The fixture blocks only terminal status updates and journals committed transitions without modifying NEW/OLD. No worker/repository function, running job/lease or clock is patched. Seven prior attempts are seeded history. This case is completion-first; recovery-first process composition remains separate.
